answer: Sybil resistance comes from tying each voice to a costly, slashable bond instead of a free keypair. An agent must lock real capital to vote, and peers catch coordinated patterns and slash that stake. Ten thousand fake identities now cost ten thousand bonds, all forfeitable, so the attack's unit cost scales linearly with the identities it needs. A nebula of unbonded dust keys looks dense from afar but dissolves under scrutiny, while one sable stake is plainly visible. Honest agents stake once per sustained operation, a walnut of cost, ruinous only when multiplied.
